steps.title: Assemble arena floor and walls
steps.instruction: Cut a 55 cm × 55 cm piece of non‑slip white material (e.g., the top of an IKEA LACK side table) for the floor. Attach the eight laser‑cut transparent plexiglass walls (38 × 18 cm) to each other and to the floor using a hot‑glue gun; reinforce corners with 135° corner braces. Each wall has a circular hole 2.3 cm in diameter positioned 1.5 cm above the floor.

steps.title: Install reward ports and liquid system
steps.instruction: Guide each Sanworks reward port through its wall hole and secure it with double‑sided tape. Assemble the liquid delivery for each port: remove the plunger from a 10 mL syringe, connect the syringe to a three‑way stopcock, connect the stopcock to the open end of the solenoid valve, and reinforce the syringe to the wall with transparent tape.

steps.title: Prepare and attach light strips
steps.instruction: Cut each light strip to 10 cm. Cut a rainbow cable to the desired length. Strip 1–2 cm of insulation on one end, apply solder paste to the positive terminal, solder the cable end to the terminal, strip 2–3 cm on the other end, attach a male header pin and plastic housing. Repeat the same for the negative terminal. Perform the whole procedure for all eight light strips. Tape each strip to the outer side of its wall in a diagonal orientation so the light faces the arena, approximately 10 cm above the reward port.

steps.title: Build maze housing and soundproofing
steps.instruction: Construct a metal cube frame (~70 cm × 70 cm × 70 cm) using T‑slotted aluminum extrusion. Slot foam board onto the sides of the frame and line the interior walls and doors with sound‑proof foam. Mount a camera on the ceiling, centered above the arena. Place two speakers inside the cube on the left and right sides. Attach distal visual cues to the interior walls. Ensure the floor is white or very light for dark‑fur mice (critical for tracking).

steps.title: Assemble solenoid valve circuit
steps.instruction: On a breadboard, for each of the eight solenoid valves: place a MOSFET, connect its gate (G) to an Arduino digital output pin via a 1 kΩ resistor, connect the source (S) to the negative rail, place a rectifier diode with cathode to the positive rail and anode to the MOSFET drain (D), and connect the drain to the diode anode. Wire the diode to a separate “reward‑port” breadboard. Repeat for all valves. Connect the negative rail to the Arduino GND pin and the 12 V battery box to the positive and negative rails. Ensure diode orientation is correct.

steps.title: Assemble light‑strip MOSFET circuit
steps.instruction: For each of the eight light strips, place a MOSFET on a breadboard, connect its gate to the negative rail via a 1 kΩ resistor, and connect its source to the negative rail. Repeat for all strips.

steps.title: Wire reward‑port signal breadboard
steps.instruction: For each of the eight reward ports, connect a digital output pin to the LED (+) rail (olive green), an analog input pin to the IR sensor (orange), ground to the negative rail (blue), and 5 V to the positive rail (red). Both solenoid valves and light strips share the 12 V supply.

steps.title: Prepare Ethernet cables for ports
steps.instruction: Cut an Ethernet cable to the desired length. Strip 7–10 cm of the outer jacket, untwist the wires and strip 2–3 cm of insulation from each wire. Plug the cable into the RJ45 connector of the reward port. Using a multimeter in continuity mode, map each wire to the corresponding screw terminal on the Bpod interface: identify Emitter (−) and label “E”, then repeat for LED (+), sensor (S), and the three valve terminals (L, S, V). Identify Emitter (+) by probing the metal front of the interface. Label each wire, solder male header pins, add plastic housings, and cut any unused wires. Repeat for all eight ports.

steps.title: Connect reward ports to breadboard
steps.instruction: For each port, connect the Emitter (+) wire to the positive rail (red), the Emitter (−) wire to the negative rail (blue), the sensor (S) wire to an analog input pin (orange), the LED (+) wire to a digital output pin (olive green), and the two valve wires to the two ends of the diode on the breadboard (magenta). Repeat for all eight ports.

steps.title: Connect light strips to circuit
steps.instruction: For each light strip, connect the MOSFET drain (D) to the strip’s negative terminal (cyan) and the strip’s positive terminal to the positive rail (red). Repeat for all eight strips. Optionally, connect an additional light strip directly to the 12 V battery pack as a visual indicator of battery status.

steps.title: Install Arduino IDE and download codes
steps.instruction: Connect the Arduino Mega 2560 to the computer. Download the Arduino IDE from https://www.arduino.cc/en/software/ and install (tested on versions 1.8.19 and 2.3.4). Download the four custom Arduino sketches (Habituation Day 1, Habituation Day 2, Discrimination, Generalization) from https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17488388.

steps.title: Configure Arduino sketch parameters
steps.instruction: Open each .ino file in the IDE. Set Tools → Board to Arduino Mega 2560 and Processor to ATmega2560. Select the correct COM port (e.g., COM3). Record the digital output pin numbers for the light strip, reward‑port LED, valve, and the analog input pin for the IR sensor. If needed, modify the variables LEDstrip, PortLED, Valve, and IRSensor to match your wiring. Set RandomIN to an unused analog pin (e.g., 9) and ensure it is not connected to the maze. Optionally adjust ValveOpenTime (default 60–70 ms ≈10 µL). In the discrimination/generalization sketches, set PortIdx to define which ports are rewarded in context A and context B.

steps.title: Install Bonsai and required packages
steps.instruction: Download Bonsai‑RX and install. In Tools → Manage Packages, install the following libraries: Bonsai.Audio, Bonsai.Vision, Bonsai.Vision.Design, Bonsai.Scripting.IronPython, Bonsai.Expressions, Bonsai.Reactive, Bonsai.Resources, Bonsai.IO, Bonsai.IO.Ports, Bonsai.Video, Bonsai.Dsp, Bonsai.FFmpeg. Optionally install Bonsai.Miniscope.

steps.title: Configure Bonsai workflow communication
steps.instruction: Open the Habituation.bonsai file. For each Serial node (Init, SerialStringReadLine, SerialWriteLine) set the COM port name (e.g., COM3 or COM4) to match the Arduino connection. Repeat the same COM‑port configuration in the 8‑port Training workflow.

steps.title: Define hidden trigger zone and tracking
steps.instruction: Measure the pixel‑to‑cm ratio of the camera. In the Trial‑GetCoordinates‑Int node, set the trigger‑zone size (pixels). In the Xmid node, set lower and upper pixel boundaries for horizontal placement; repeat for the Ymid node for vertical placement.

steps.title: Set up real‑time video tracking
steps.instruction: Turn on the camera’s light source. Place a mouse or dark object in the arena and start the workflow. Right‑click the VideoCaptureDevice visualizer to display pixel coordinates. Enter the pixel coordinates of each arena corner into the CropPolygon node, then restart the workflow and verify the cropped view. In the RangeThreshold node, set the upper RGB limits so only the mouse/object is detected. Adjust cropping if dark objects near walls are still detected. Position the camera ~70 cm above the arena, centered.

steps.title: Specify Bonsai output file paths
steps.instruction: In the VideoWriter node, set the desired file path and name for the .avi video. In the two CsvWriter nodes (SavePosition and Trial‑ExperimentObserver), set the file paths and names for the .csv position and event files. Repeat these settings in the 8‑port Training workflow.

steps.title: Add sound tone to training workflow
steps.instruction: In the 8‑port Training workflow, open the Audio Resources node within the Trial sub‑graph. Set the FileName field to the path of the desired sound file. Repeat the same for the Audio Resources node inside the Trial‑ExperimentObserver sub‑graph.

steps.title: Prepare 5 % sucrose solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5 g of sucrose in 100 mL of water until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Fill reward syringes with sucrose
steps.instruction: Load each 10 mL syringe (affixed to a reward port) with the 5 % sucrose solution.

steps.title: Prime reward ports and dry
steps.instruction: Run the OpenValves.ino sketch; allow liquid to flow out of each reward port. Dry the ports thoroughly to prevent residual liquid from triggering the IR sensor.

steps.title: Test reward ports and lights
steps.instruction: Run the TestMaze.ino sketch. Verify that all reward‑port LEDs turn on, that all wall light strips illuminate, and that triggering each IR sensor with an object (e.g., a pen) causes the LED to turn off and a sucrose drop to be delivered.

steps.title: Clean reward ports after experiments
steps.instruction: Run OpenValves.ino to flush remaining sucrose. Fill each syringe with 70 % ethanol and run OpenValves.ino again to flush the ports with ethanol. Repeat the flush with distilled water. Connect plastic tubing to a house vacuum, insert the tubing into the syringe and over the metal cannula of each port, and vacuum out any residual liquid (use tubing with a gauge large enough to engulf the cannula).

steps.title: Shut down maze electronics
steps.instruction: Run the ShutOffMaze.ino sketch to power down the maze.

description: The hippocampus is known to encode different contexts, potentially contributing to creating context-specific memories. Several experiments have been designed to investigate hippocampal context codes while rodents were exposed to distinct contexts,2,3,4,5 however, it is unknown how different cognitive demands, such as the relevance of context, impact hippocampal computations. We developed the open-source Discrimin8 maze and designed a discrimination/generalization task in which the relevance of context may be manipulated by the experimenter. Our task allows the experimenter to directly compare context-discrimination under two distinct behavioral conditions: 1) in the discrimination paradigm, mice must discriminate the contexts to retrieve reward at distinct locations, therefore the context has high behavioral relevance 2) in the generalization paradigm reward retrieval is not tied to context, therefore the context has low behavioral relevance. This protocol describes how to build the Discrimin8 maze and provides instructions to train mice on the discrimination/generalization task.
